commits.message:
A Progress is timed on the host that draws it (rich-animation-42lg.1t6)

A Progress read its own clock inside render, so a frame drawn for one
moment got cells stamped for another, and a paused host could not hold it.
Now every time a Progress keeps or draws at — a task's start, each update,
a finish, a refill's start, the frame — is one host's frameTime: its own
Live, or the host given as `drawnBy` (a Live, an App, a WidgetApp).

RenderOptions.frameTime becomes `frame: { time, host }`, so a frame's time
always comes with the host it belongs to, and a Progress drawn in a frame of
any other host throws instead of showing elapsed time from another clock.
A print reads the host's frameTime, so elapsed is right as it prints. Run
backwards, a task drawn before its start has not started, and speed spans
the earliest to the latest sample.

Breaking: a default Progress inside another host's view now throws; give it
`drawnBy`. The docs Group examples, showcase, rich-dash and rich-explore do,
and e2e runs the three docs examples.

Reduced motion stops the terminal's blink attribute (rich-animation-42lg.xbt) (#497)

* Reduced motion stops the terminal's blink attribute (rich-animation-42lg.xbt)

A reduced-motion console still wrote SGR 5 for `[blink]`, which the
terminal animates on its own. The reader's preference now lives on
`Destination` (`reducedMotion`), resolved once by `resolveDestination`;
each host's `RenderOptions.reducedMotion` reads it back from there.
`shownOn` unsets blink and blink2 (`Style.reduced()`) for the one encoder
and for a recording console, so print, Live/App frames, renderToString
and the HTML/SVG/text exports all show the text steady. Drawing could not
do it: the console lays its print and base styles on after render.

* Blink is taken out of what is painted and recorded, once (rich-animation-42lg.xbt)

Review (high) fixes:
- SurfacePainter.paint returns its rows as the destination shows them, so
  App.frame and paint handlers carry no blink under reduced motion.
- Console maps each write through shownOn once, then records and encodes it.
- A hand-made encode takes the preference on its Destination (docs).
- Stale descriptions of Destination in console.md, the destination getter
  and render.ts's header name reducedMotion.
- The test helper encodes with the preference it drew under.
